title: The Aurora Breach
brief: Three o'clock in the morning and Aurora is on fire. One attacker chained three separate weaknesses: they read the customer table, they got their code running in a signed-in session, and they used that session to change an account. Each foothold made the next one easier. Close all three and the chain breaks anywhere you cut it — but a partial fix leaves them a way back in.
hints: These are three different bugs, not one bug in three places. The fix that works for the database will not help the browser.
Work out what each stage trusts that it should not. The query trusts a search term, the page trusts a review, the endpoint trusts that a request came from Aurora.
Every technique you need has appeared before. The difficulty is recognising which one belongs where.

stages.title: They read the customer table
stages.brief: The order lookup builds its query by hand. The attacker used it to read a table it was never meant to touch.

stages.title: They got code running in a signed-in session
stages.brief: The order history page writes the delivery note straight into the document. That is where the attacker's script ran, inside a real customer's session.

stages.title: They used that session to change an account
stages.brief: With code running in the customer's page, the attacker made their browser post a new payout account. The endpoint asked for nothing but the cookie the browser was already sending.
